To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
water politics in Israel in the 195os were not only about the struggle over the control of water resources and water management.
the Israeli state, as an actor in the water sector, did not emerge in 1948, but was constructed over the course of the 1950's.

(1) Israeli water politics in the 195os were shaped by the internal politics of the state and its institutions; (2) the state's intervention in the civil sphere was not a given but a contested issue that was resolved only in the mid-195os; and (3) the notion that water was a scarce resource was established in the mid- to late-1950s and not before.
In summary, our research is concerned with
locating the fragments of the state in its early years and the limits of state power.
locating the fragments of the state in order to understand the limits of its authority.
the politics of the state and not only its policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Israeli water policies were the outcome of the interplay between internal and external factors and between the state and civil society.
the Israeli state was a work in progress, and that water was a key site for working out the limits of the state.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water is a political resource, and that the political nature of water is a function of the social, political, and economic relations in which it is embedded.
water politics in Israel during the early years were about the state's struggle to locate itself in the political and cultural landscape, as well as the limits of its authority and legitimacy.
we have shown the limits of the state in its early years and the ways in which the state was formed by the struggle over water and the struggle over the meanings of water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of water policymaking in Israel during its formative years offers a new perspective for the study of the Israeli state and its limits.
the state, its boundaries, and its limits are never fixed.
water politics is not merely a technical and administrative issue, but rather, it is an arena in which the state's boundaries and its relationship to civil society are constantly being negotiated.
